lawyer:
Swapan Kumar Mitra, Advocate—For the Petitioners.
HN Nondy, Advocate —For the Opposite Party.
parties:
Ashrafunnessa & others ------ Petitioners
vs
Bimsankar, Shiba Bigraha and another ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
This rule on an application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure at the instance of Ashrafunnessa and others arises from the order No. 10 dated 27-9-2000 passed by the learned District Judge, Dhaka in Transfer Miscellaneous case No. 42 of 2000, allowing the Miscellaneous case and transferring the SCC Suit No. 20 of 1998 of the Court of 6th Assistant Judge and Title Suit No. 145 of the Court of 3rd Additional Assistant Judge, Dhaka to the Court of 1st Subordinate Judge, Dhaka for simultaneous hearing with Title Suit No.  240 of 1997 pending in the Court of 1st Subordinate Judge, Dhaka.

2. The opposite party No. 1 filed a transfer Miscellaneous Case No. 42 of 2000 in the Court of District Judge, Dhaka against the petitioners and opposite party No. 2 for transferring SCC Suit No. 20 of 1998 of the Court of 6th Assistant Judge, Dhaka and Title Suit No. 145 of 1997 of the Court of 3rd Additional Assistant Judge, Dhaka to the Court of 1st Subordinate Judge, Dhaka for hearing along with Title Suit No. 240 of 1997 pending in the said Court.

3. The case of the opposite party is that the land comprises in Mouza Shahar Dhaka CS Khatian No. 3926, plot No. 150 area 0616 Ajutansha, originally belonged to Sree Mata Sarajani Daisha, who by registered deed No. 274 dated 11-1-1922 transferred the said land to Sreejukta Rudra Tridandi Tripur Linga Swami and thereafter Swamji transferred the same to plaintiff Bigraha by will and the executors filed a probate case in the Court of learned district Judge and got an order and was possessing the land through tenants and that the predecessor of petitioner and opposite party No. 2,was a ten-ant under them and to grab the said property he managed to get the SA record in his name in collusion with the employees of settlement office and the opposite party No. 1 on 31-12-1996 came to know that SA record of the suit land has been prepared in the name of predecessor of the petitioner and, as such, the opposite party No.  1 has filed Title Suit No. 240 of 1997 in the Court of the first Subordinate Judge, Dhaka for correction of record; that the predecessor of the petitioner is a defaulter in respect of payment of rent and, as such, the opposite party No. 1 has filed SCC Suit No. 20 of 1998 in the Court of the 6th Assistant Judge Dhaka for the eviction of the petitioners; that the petitioners were taking steps for construction of new building in the suit land after demolishing the old and dilapidated building and, as such, the opposite party No. 1 has filed Title Suit No. 37 of 1996 for permanent injunction and the said suit has been transferred to the Court 3rd Additional Assistant Judge, and has been renumbered as Title Suit No. 145 of 1997 and these 3 suits are pending 3 different Courts though the suit property and plaintiffs and defendants are same and, as such, all three suits should be heard by the learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Court Dhaka.

4. The petitioners contested the case by filing written objection denying the material allegations made in the case and their further case is that the nature of 3 suits are different and the parties of the suits are also different, that/Title Suit. No. 145 of 1997 (Title Suit No. 37 of 1996) is a suit for permanent injunction and defendant No. 4 Tofazzal Hossain, son of late Arab Ali, is not a party in Title Suit No. 240 of 1997 and in SCC Suit No. 20 of 1998 and there title Suit No. 145 of 1997 is fixed for hearing and in these suits, the opposite party No. 1 filed an application for temporary injunction which was rejected by the learned Assistant Judge and against that, the plaintiff opposite party No. 1 preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No. 303 of 1997 in the Court of learned District Judge Dhaka who after hearing dismissed the appeal; that Title Suit No. 140 of 1997 pending in, the Court of 1st Subordinate Judge, Dhaka is fixed for filling written statements and SCC suit No. 20 of 1998 is fixed for return of summons as because the summons of said suit has not yet been served upon the petitioners, that the nature of all 3 suits are not similar and there is no land-lord and tenancy relationship between the plaintiffs and defendants; that there is no con-tract and there is no rent receipts and these petitioners are not tenants under the plaintiff opposite party and, as such, since the parities not same and nature of the suits are different, there is no scope for hearing all the three suits by one Court.

5. Learned District Judge after hearing by his judgment and order dated 27-9-2000 allowed the Transfer Miscellaneous Case No. 42 of 2000.

6. Being aggrieved by an dissatisfied with the order dated 27-9-2000 passed by the learned District Judge, Dhaka, the petitioner moved this revisional application before this Court and obtained the present Rule.

7. Mr Swapan Kumar Mitra, the learned Advocate for the petitioners submits that Title Suit No. 145 of 1997 (TS No. 37 of 1996) is a suit for permanent injunction and the parties of the suit are different. Moreover their suits are fixed for hearing and, as such, the learned District Judge committed illegality in transferring the suit for simultaneous hearing along with other two suit while these two suits are fixed for service of notice and for filing for written statements. He further submits that Title Suit No. 240 of 1997 is a suit for declaration of title. Title suit No. 145 of 1997 is a suit for permanent injunction and SCC suit No. 20 of 1998 is a suit for eviction of tenants and thus the nature of all these three suits are not same. It is further submitted that the learned District judge committed illegality in directing to try these three suits simultaneously without taking into consideration that Title Suit No. 240 of 1997 and SCC Suit No. 20 of 1998 are at a preliminary stage and it would come long delay to reach at the hearing stage for disposal along with Title Suit No. 145 of 1997 and, as such, the impugned order is liable to be set aside.

8. Mr HN Nondy, the learned Advocate for the opposite party on the order hand submits that these three suits are pending in different Courts though the suit properties and the plaintiff and defendants are same as such all these three suits should be heard by the learned Subordinate Judge first Court and the impugned order passed by the learned District Judge is legal and he did not commit any illegality in passing the impugned order.

9. The point for determination is to whether the learned District Judge has committed any illegality in passing the impugned order No. 10 dated 27-9-2000 in transferring the Miscellaneous case No. 42 of 2000 and SCC suit No. 20 of 1998 with Title Suit No. 240 of 1997 pending in the Court of Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka whether the petitioner is entitled to get any relief in this rule as prayed for.

<u>10. In the light of the above facts and circumstances of the case, it appears that Title Suit No. 145 of 1997 is a suit permanent injunction and the parties of the suit are different and other two suits are not of the same stage. It further appears from the evidence on record that Title Suit No. 240 of 1997 is a suit for declaration of title and Title Suit No. 145 of 1997 is a suit for permanent injunction and SCC suit No. 20 of 1998 is a suit for eviction of tenants and thus the nature of all three suits are different. Thus from the facts and circumstances of the case, it appears that the learned District Judge committed wrong in directing to try these three suits simultaneously without taking into consideration that Title Suit No. 240 of 1997 and SCC Suit No. 20 of 1998 at preliminary stage and it will take long time to reach at the hearing stage for disposal along with Title Suit No. 145 of 1997 and, as such, the order No. 10 dated 27-9-2000 passed by the learned District Judge is not legal and thus he has committed an error of law in passing the impugned order.</u>

11. It appears that the suits are long, which should be dispose of expeditiously. So the concerned Judge of the Courts where in above mentioned suits are pending are directed to dispose of the above mentioned suits expeditiously preferably within 6 (six) months from the date of receipt of this order without allowing any adjournment to any parties.

In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to cost with a direction to dispose of the SCC Suit No. 20 of 1998. Title Suit No. 145 of 1997 and Title Suit No. 240 of 1997 preferably within 6(six) months from the date of receipt of this order. Let a copy of this order be sent to the concerned Courts for compliance.

End.
